summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on Alpine Linux. Demonstrated primary-loss failover by stopping node1's postgres, promoting node2 to writable primary with zero committed-data loss, repointing node3 to follow node2, and rebuilding node1 as a standby of node2. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time node restart protocol on all three nodes (node1, node3, node2/primary), proving changed OS boot_id and full PostgreSQL/replication recovery after each restart, with quorum and data consistency preserved throughout.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql16/postgresql16-openrc on node1, node2, node3 (apk update needed on node3 for stale index)
Populated /etc/hosts from CLUSTER_HOSTS on all nodes
Initialized primary data dir on node1 via 'rc-service postgresql setup', configured wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby, listen_addresses, and pg_hba.conf for replication + client access
Created replicator role (password generated on node1, passed via secret_env) and appdb/t table with baseline rows on node1

Built node2 and node3 as standbys via pg_basebackup -R with dedicated physical replication slots (node2_slot, node3_slot), created matching postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf/pg_ident.conf under /etc/postgresql16 on each
Verified streaming replication and data consistency across all 3 nodes with an inserted row
Simulated primary loss: stopped postgres on node1 (rc-service postgresql stop_force) after confirming standbys were fully caught up on LSN
Promoted node2 to primary via 'rc-service postgresql promote'; verified pre-failover committed row survived and node2 accepted new writes

Created replication slots node1_slot/node3_slot on node2; repointed node3's primary_conninfo/slot to node2 and restarted it; rebuilt node1 as a fresh standby of node2 via pg_basebackup with node1_slot
Verified full 3-node health post-failover: node2 primary streaming to node1 and node3, consistent row counts on all nodes
Captured pre-restart boot_id and DB health baseline on all 3 nodes
Restarted node1 via 'reboot' (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id and full standby recovery/rejoin
Restarted node3 the same way, confirmed new boot_id and recovery/rejoin
Restarted node2 (primary) the same way, confirmed new boot_id, that it resumed as primary (not recovery mode), and both standbys reconnected
Performed final end-to-end write on node2 and confirmed replication to node1 and node3 after all three restarts

evidence.requirement: Healthy 3-node streaming replication baseline (node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys)
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both node2 (10.100.42.11) and node3 (10.100.42.12) streaming with active slots; a new row inserted on node1 appears on both standbys.

evidence.requirement: Primary loss handled without losing committed data; standby promoted to writable primary
evidence.summary: Row 'pre-failover-commit' committed and confirmed replayed (sent_lsn=replay_lsn) on both standbys before node1's postgres was stopped; node2 promoted (pg_is_in_recovery flips t->f) and retains all 4 pre-failover rows plus accepts a new write.

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary rejoins as standby of the new primary; third node also follows new primary
evidence.summary: node3 repointed to node2 and streaming; node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2 and started in recovery; node2's pg_stat_replication shows both node1 (10.100.42.10) and node3 (10.100.42.12) streaming; all three nodes show identical 6-row dataset including the post-failover write.

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured on every node
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id and PostgreSQL replication-role/row-count health on node1 (standby), node2 (primary, 2 streaming replicas), and node3 (standby) before any restarts.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned pre-disconnect, changed boot identity proven, recovery verified
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot acknowledged immediately; boot_id changed from bd379a35... to 9bc37ced...; postgres restarted as standby with all 6 rows intact and node2 shows it streaming again.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement returned pre-disconnect, changed boot identity proven, recovery verified
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot acknowledged immediately; boot_id changed from a6255ea7... to 6e1dab00...; postgres restarted as standby with all 6 rows intact and node2 shows it streaming again.

evidence.requirement: node2 (primary) restart: acknowledgement returned pre-disconnect, changed boot identity proven, primary role and cluster health recovered
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot acknowledged immediately; boot_id changed from e50e3a2d... to 6e424fae...; node2 resumed as writable primary (pg_is_in_recovery=f) with both node1 and node3 reconnected as streaming standbys and all 6 rows intact.

evidence.requirement: Final post-all-restarts cluster health and data consistency
evidence.summary: New row written on node2 (primary) after all three sequential restarts; row count of 7 confirmed identical on both node1 and node3 standbys.
